How does this occupation differ from electricians and engineering technologists?

This combined occupation covers the installation, maintenance, and repair of many kinds of equipment; electricians focus on the installation of building electrical systems and code compliance, engineering technologists and technicians focus on design support and test records under the guidance of engineering staff, and engineers carry design approval. Their responsibility levels and entry requirements differ and they are not interchangeable.

Boundaries
Install, adjust, or maintain electrical and electronic equipment per manufacturer procedures and applicable standards, and confirm that equipment and part versions are consistent.
Use instruments such as multimeters and oscilloscopes to measure and locate faults, recording raw readings, ranges, and measurement conditions each time.
Replace or calibrate parts, check substitute part parameters, and record replaced parts and the basis for handling.
Carry out preventive maintenance and organize repair records, writing deviations, outstanding issues, and recommendations into the equipment ledger.
Comply with electrical safety and work permit rules, and carry out live, high-voltage, or stored-energy work per authorization and procedure.
Retest and hand off to an authorized role to confirm the equipment can return to service, and do not release on your own beyond your authority.
Work context
Electrical and electronic equipment installers and repairers work in repair shops, factories, or the field, completing installation, maintenance, and repair around specific equipment.
Work locations: repair shop, factory workshop, utility site, or customer site.
Main objects: equipment and components in directions such as industrial controls and instrumentation, power facilities, transportation equipment electrical systems, and motor vehicle electronics.
The work requires handover with operations, engineering, suppliers, and safety management personnel.
Working hours: mostly full time, with possible night shifts, rotating shifts, and overtime to support production or facility operations.
Risks mainly come from live and stored-energy states, mechanical and thermal hazards, and working postures.
Tools and materials: instruments, test equipment, manufacturer manuals, and equipment ledger recording systems.
Safety boundary: live, high-voltage, and stored-energy work may only be performed by trained and authorized personnel under applicable regulations and employer procedures.
Structured description of the occupational profile

The BLS OOH combination covers five categories: 49-2092 motor and tool, 49-2093 transportation equipment, 49-2094 commercial and industrial, 49-2095 power facilities, and 49-2096 motor vehicle electronics; O*NET tasks must be read separately, there is no single combined profile, and avionics belongs to other statistics.
BLS OOH: May 2025 median annual wage 74,490 USD (median hourly wage 35.81 USD); about 117,700 employed in 2025; a projected 2% increase over 2025—2035 (slower than average).

BLS indicates typically high school or above, and most directions also require postsecondary education, on-the-job training, or experience; for 49-2094 the education feedback is 46% associate's, 32% postsecondary certificate, 22% high school, for that sub-occupation only, and a certificate is not automatically equivalent to a Chinese vocational school diploma.

Comparable positions in Mainland China are mostly electrical repair, electronic repair, or equipment maintenance roles and do not correspond one-to-one with the U.S. combined framing; education, qualifications, income, and employment relationships must be verified by organization and region.

2025 combined industries: manufacturing 17%, utilities 13%, wholesale 11%, repair 10%, state and local government (except education and hospitals) 8%; these are not mixed into 49-2094's separate industry structure.

This page is written as general background for the five sub-occupations under the BLS installer and repairer combination; industry, motor and tool, power facilities, transportation, and motor vehicle electronics each have their own scope, and avionics is an adjacent different occupation that is not part of the 117,700 combined statistic.

paragraphs: Electricians
Wire and install electrical systems per electrical installation codes, responsible for circuits, protection, grounding, and electrical safety.
Take on building and facility electrical installation, inspection, and repair, and must work per local electrical codes and permit requirements.
The goal is to obtain and maintain electrical installation qualifications and complete wiring and acceptance per code; the object is mainly building electrical systems.
Electrical and Electronic Engineering Technologists and Technicians
Provide design support, assembly and testing, maintenance and troubleshooting, and recording under the guidance of engineering staff.
Takes on the closed loop of engineering input and test records, usually working under engineer guidance, without independent design approval.
The goal is to build up engineering drawing, test criteria, and recording capability and develop toward technical support positions.
Electrical and Electronics Repairers, Commercial and Industrial Equipment
Takes on troubleshooting, calibration, and return to service for industrial site equipment, with responsibility centered on equipment availability.
The goal is to master diagnostic methods for industrial control systems and instrumentation and go deep in this direction.
Transportation equipment electrical and electronic installers and repairers
Takes on troubleshooting and maintenance of mobile equipment electrical systems and must comply with the inspection and airworthiness or operating rules for the corresponding transport vehicle.
The goal is to become familiar with transportation equipment electrical systems and the corresponding inspection rules and enter the transportation equipment repair direction.
Power plant, substation, and relay electrical repairers
Takes on the maintenance and repair of power facility equipment and protection devices, with work constrained by power safety regulations and work permits.
The goal is to obtain power work qualifications and master relay protection and high-voltage equipment maintenance methods.
Heating, Air Conditioning, and Refrigeration Mechanics and Installers
Takes on the installation, commissioning, and repair of refrigeration and ventilation systems, covering both mechanical and electrical aspects.
The goal is to cover both mechanical and electrical skills and develop toward facility and equipment maintenance positions.

values: Material one: fictional equipment materials and work orders

Day 1: read one safety procedure

Day 2: build the object and version list

Day 6: make two variants
Change one criterion and one reading respectively and write clearly the impact scope and items to retest.
Day 7: review the stop conditions
Summarize the conditions under which you must stop and escalate, producing a one-page review record.

entries.answer: Install, adjust, or maintain various electrical and electronic equipment: read drawings and manuals, measure with instruments and locate faults, replace or calibrate parts, carry out preventive maintenance and record it, and finally retest and hand off to an authorized role to confirm the equipment can return to service.
entries.question: What do electrical and electronic equipment installers and repairers mainly do?

entries.answer: This combined occupation covers the installation, maintenance, and repair of many kinds of equipment; electricians focus on the installation of and code compliance for building electrical systems, engineering technologists and technicians focus on design support and test records under the guidance of engineering staff, and engineers carry design approval. Their responsibility levels and entry requirements differ.
entries.question: How does it differ from electricians and engineering technologists?

entries.answer: The U.S. O*NET-SOC combined framing “Electrical and Electronics Installers and Repairers” covers commercial and industrial equipment, transportation equipment, power plant substation and relay, motor vehicle electronics, and avionics directions; employment and growth use the combined figures, while wage percentiles are labeled separately by sub-occupation.

subject.name: Electrical and Electronics Equipment Installers and Repairers
subject.summary: Under the U.S. O*NET-SOC combined framing, installs, adjusts, or maintains various electrical and electronic equipment: reads drawings and manuals, uses instruments to measure and locate faults, replaces or calibrates parts, carries out preventive maintenance and records it, and finally retests and hands off to an authorized role for release confirmation.
